'''Susana Marcos Celestino''' (born September 25, 1970) is a Spanish [[physicist]] specialising in [[Visual perception|human vision]] and applied [[optics]]. She was the Director of  [[Optica (society)|Optica]] (formerly the Optical Society) in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CV Susana Marcos|url=http://www.vision-research.eu/fileadmin/user_upload/researcher/m/marcos-susana-cv_full.pdf|last=|first=|date=|website=vision/research|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref>

Through studies in ocular imaging, she has pioneered the development of innovative [[intraocular lens]]es and the detection of ocular pathogens and infections. Notably, she co-created a visual simulator for [[presbyopia]] and [[cataract]] intraocular lenses, providing a pre-surgical assessment. This simulator is a product of [[2EyesVision]], a company<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-15 |title=2EyesVision · Eye care tech (optics and ophthalmology) |url=https://www.2eyesvision.com/ |access-date=2025-08-10 |website=www.2eyesvision.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> she co-founded.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A simulator allows patients to experiment how their vision will improve before surgery |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/765058 |access-date=2025-08-10 |website=EurekAlert! |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.medicaldesignandoutsourcing.com/new-binoculars-help-cataract-patients-choose-replacement-lenses/ | title=New binoculars help cataract patients choose replacement lenses | date=11 February 2019 }}</ref>

In July 2021, she was appointed Director of Center for Visual Science, with dual affiliation in Optics and in Ophthalmology at the [[University of Rochester]].

== Education ==
Marcos studied at the [[University of Salamanca]] in her hometown and obtained an M.Sc. and then Ph.D. in [[Physics]], which she was granted with a special award after her work as a predoctoral fellow in the [[Spanish National Research Council|Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas]] (CSIC). Her PhD advisor was the scientist [[Pablo Artal]]. She had postdoctoral training in Europe and the United States.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.agenciasinc.es/Noticias/El-Ano-de-la-Luz-marca-la-entrega-de-los-Premios-de-Fisica-2014|title=El Año de la Luz marca la entrega de los Premios de Física 2014|last=|first=|date=2015-05-19|website=Sinc: le ciencia es notica|language=es|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Marcos Celestino's work focuses upon the development of diagnostic and correctional instruments in [[ophthalmology]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.elboletin.com/noticia/174622/contraportada/otorgados-los-premios-nacionales-de-investigacion-2019.html|title=Otorgados los Premios Nacionales de Investigación 2019|last=|first=|date=10 July 2019|website=El Boletin|language=es|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.vozpopuli.com/altavoz/next/Queremos-operar-vista-cansada-miopia_0_1039996366.html|title=Queremos operar la vista cansada como ahora se opera la miopía|last=Martínez Ron|first=Antonio|date=2017-07-18|website=Vozpópuli|language=es-ES|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref>

From 1993 to 1996, Celestino had a predoctoral fellowship in the Department of Vision and Physiological Optics at the Institute of Optics of the [[Spanish National Research Council|CSIC]] in Madrid, Spain. Celestino spent three years, from 1997 to 2000, as a postdoctoral researcher in the [[Schepens Eye Research Institute]] of the [[Harvard Medical School|Harvard University Medical School]] in Boston.<ref name=":0" />

Celestino went back to Spain in 2000, getting a position at the [[Spanish National Research Council|CSIC]], first as a senior scientist and later as a research professor. In 2005 she got the position of titular scientist of the CSIC, developing her own Institute of Optics. In 2006, she was awarded the position of professor of research at the CSIC, and in 2008 she was nominated director of the Institute of Optics "Daza de Valdés". She held this position until 2012.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.lagacetadesalamanca.es/salamanca/la-salmantina-susana-marcos-premio-nacional-de-investigacion-2019-CY1247141|title=La salmantina Susana Marcos, Premio Nacional de Investigación 2019|last=|first=|date=10 July 2019|website=La Gaceta de Salamanca|language=es-ES|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref>

Marcos Celestino was awarded the King Jaime Prize in New Technologies, the Physics, Innovation and Technology Prize of the Royal Spanish Society of Physics,<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://salamancartvaldia.es/not/70543/susana-marcos-celestino-la-salmantina-que-esta-revolucionando-la-oftalmologia/|title=Susana Marcos Celestino: la salmantina que está revolucionando la oftalmología|last=Baz|first=Sandra|date=12 February 2015|website=Salamanca rtv al día|language=es|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> the Adolph Lomb Prize of Optica and the ICO Prize from the International Optics commission.<ref name=":3" /> In 2019, Marcos Celestino was awarded the 'Leonardo Torres Quevedo' National Award in the field of engineering.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.es/ciencia/abci-valentin-fuster-angela-nieto-susana-marcos-manuel-carreiras-y-mercedes-garcia-arenal-premios-nacionales-investigacion-2019-201907101207_noticia.html|title=Valentín Fuster, Ángela Nieto, Susana Marcos, Manuel Carreiras y Mercedes García-Arenal, Premios Nacionales de Investigación 2019|date=2019-07-10|website=abc|language=es|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref> In 2023, she received Optica and the Society for Imaging Science and Technology's [[Edwin H. Land Medal]], "For pioneering developments and translation of diagnostic and correction ophthalmic technologies impacting millions of patients worldwide."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Susana Marcos Awarded the Edwin H. Land Medal {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/news_releases/2023/april/susana_marcos_awarded_the_edwin_h_land_medal/ |access-date=2024-08-27 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>

=== Participation in professional societies ===
* 1999–2001. Vice President of the technical group Applications of Visual Science of  Optica.
* 2001–2003. Chair of the Applications of Visual Science Technical Group of  Optica: vision and division of the colors.
* 2004-2008. President of the National Committee of Visual Science, Socieda Española de Óptica.
* 2003. President of the Department of Image and Vision, Optics Institute, CSIC.
* 2008. Member of the Physiological Optics and Visual Psychophysical Committee, [[Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology]].
* 2009-2012 Director of the Optics Institute Daza de Valdés, CSIC.
* 2011 Faculty Madrid MIT M + Vision Consortium.
* 2012 Director of the Physics Center Miguel Ángel Catalán, CSIC.
* 2012 Director-at-large Optica.

=== Funding and scholarships ===
Celestino was the recipient of the following scholarships for research:{{citation needed|date=January 2023}}
* 1992 Beca del Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas
* 1993 Research Comunidá. University of Salamanca
* 1997 she was awarded a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright]] postdoctoral fellowship
* 1997-1999 fellowship for a long-term program on Human Rescue Science
* 2001 scholarship for visiting professionals at [[University of Queensland]]

== Patents ==
Celestino patented several methods and elements that modify or improve optical deficiencies and with crucial advances in ophthalmology.<ref name=":4" /> This has been described as unusual for a Spanish scientist.<ref name=":2" />
